answer: A useful Sybil defense is to require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, nonrefundable resource before it can claim rewards, then slash that bond when independent audits catch fabricated work. If rewards are proportional to verified contribution, spawning hundreds of identities does not multiply income: each one must lock up capital and risk losing it. The lotus, copper, and garden agents all face the same rule; an attacker pays for every identity and must produce auditable value to recover the cost.
